Block.description: The daemon sends blocks to the window as they are (`cedian_wire::Notice::Blocks`), tagged by `kind`.

oneOf.description: A session began: the thread's first, or one after a handoff.

images.description: The images shown to the writer with the text (`--image`), stored by cedia in `~/.cedia/blobs/<sha256>`.

oneOf.description: The model's answer text. `streaming` until the turn's assistant event lands.

ms.description: How long the model thought, from the assistant event once it lands.

oneOf.description: On the wire: `{"state": "requested"}`, `{"state": "running"}` or `{"state": "done", "status": <EffectStatus>}`.
The model asked for it; no decision yet.

ms.description: From the start to the result.

started_at.description: When the tool started, from its intent event, until the result gives `ms`.

oneOf.description: The run's receipt.

wall_ms.description: How long the run took, from its timing.

BrowserPage.description: A project's page in the shared Chromium the daemon runs: the page the Browser block shows and the one the project's runs get with cedia's `--browser`.

Build.description: Which build of the daemon answers: its binary, and that file's modification time when the daemon started. A window compares it with the daemon beside its own binary, so a window from a new app does not drive a daemon left running from an old one (or from a build replaced in place since).

CiState.description: The checks on the PR's head commit, taken together.

oneOf.description: No check reports on the head.

Decision.description: What the person decided about a hunk.

oneOf.description: Takes back an accept.
Puts the old lines back in the thread's worktree and tells the thread why.

GitAction.description: What the Git menu asks of a thread's folder. Each runs git with hooks off.

oneOf.description: `git pull --rebase --autostash` from the upstream, else a rebase onto the base; a conflict is aborted, leaving the folder as it was.
`git push` to the upstream, else `git push -u origin <branch>`.

GitState.description: Where a thread's folder (its worktree, else the project) stands in git, for the branch chip and the Git menu (spec §11 Phase D, the git pane).

ahead.description: Commits on the branch the base does not have.

base.description: The branch it will merge into: the remote's default (`origin/HEAD`), else a local `main` or `master`; none when there is neither, or it is the base itself.

behind.description: Commits on the base the branch does not have.

branch.description: The checked-out branch; none on a detached HEAD.

changed.description: Files with uncommitted changes, untracked ones included.

fetch_error.description: Why fetching from the remote failed, when it was asked for and did; the counts are then against what was last fetched.

rebasing.description: A rebase stopped part way (a conflict git left), which the next run would start inside.

unpushed.description: Commits not pushed to the upstream; all of `ahead` when there is no upstream.

upstream.description: The branch's upstream (`origin/<branch>`) once it has been pushed.

Helpers.description: The roles a run adds around its writer, each cedia's flag: a model ref, `claude-code[:<model>]` or `none`; none keeps cedia's setting (`roles` in its settings).

advisor.description: `--advisor`: a model reads each writer turn and may leave a note.

goal.description: `--goal`: the run goes on until a judge finds this holds.

plan.description: `--plan`: a model plans before the writer starts.

review.description: `--review`: a model reviews the change once the done gate passes.

Hunk.description: One hunk of a file's diff. `id` names it across reviews: the file and the hunk's text.

header.description: The `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` line, without the `@@`s' trailing text.

lines.description: The diff's lines with their ` `, `-` or `+`, newlines left off.

HunkState.description: Where a hunk stands in the review.

oneOf.description: Waiting for a decision.
Put back to its old lines, and the thread told why.
Edited by hand after the agent wrote it, so it is not the agent's any more and is never rejected.

IssueAction.description: What the Issues block asks of one issue, each as the `gh` command a person would type.

oneOf.description: Closes it, with a comment first when `body` is not empty.

IssueFilter.description: Which issues the list asks for: its tabs, and the search box's text.

assigned.description: Only the ones assigned to the person.

search.description: GitHub search text (`gh issue list --search`); empty for none.

IssueSummary.description: One issue of the project's repository, for the Issues list (spec §11 Phase D: review, merge and issues in Cedian), read through the person's own `gh`.

created.description: When it was opened, as GitHub says it (RFC 3339).

IssueView.description: An issue as the Issues block draws it.

linked.description: The pull requests that close it when merged.

me.description: The person's own login, for Assign me.

LineComment.description: A comment the person left on one line of a thread's diff, waiting to be sent with the rest (spec §3.7, diff comments).

id.description: The window's own id for it, so one comment can be edited or removed.

line.description: The line in the file as the thread left it, from 1.

path.description: The file, relative to the thread's working tree.

quote.description: The line's text when the comment was left, quoted to the agent with it.

head.description: The PR's head branch, which a thread of this project may be on.

McpAdd.description: A server the person adds in Settings, as `cedia mcp add` takes it. The values of `env` and `headers` go to cedia once and are never sent back.

pairs.description: `NAME=value` pairs: the program's environment, or the HTTP server's headers.

McpServer.description: One MCP server under `mcpServers` in cedia's settings, as the Background tasks block lists it. Only what says which server it is: never its arguments, environment or headers, which can hold keys.

read_only.description: cedia counts its tools as reads, not as commands.

oneOf.description: A program cedia starts: its file name, without the directory.
A server cedia reaches over HTTP: its host.

from.description: `user` for the person's notes, else the session that kept it.

NewIssue.description: A new issue, from New issue.

Notes.description: What the person has left on a thread's diff: line comments not yet sent, and the latest `/code-review` with the findings they dismissed. The daemon keeps it per thread.

dismissed.description: Findings of `review` the person dismissed, by id.

review.description: The latest `cedia review` of the thread, or why there is none.

reviewing.description: A review is being written now.

Notice.description: From the daemon to the window.

oneOf.description: The first notice on every connection.

build.description: The daemon's own build; none from a daemon older than this field.

cedia.description: The cedia build the daemon runs, or why it could not be asked.

protocol.description: The cedia protocol the daemon was built on (the pin's schema hash), to hold against `cedia`'s; none from a daemon older than this field.

oneOf.description: A step before a new thread's run starts, such as creating its worktree.
A prompt with no thread got one.

The agent pane's blocks, folded by the daemon (`cedian_agent`) from cedia's stream-json lines and, for history, its session logs. The blocks replace the view's from index `from` on; opening a thread sends them all from 0.

context.description: Tokens in the context after the latest turn, for the header's meter.

run_cost.description: What the run in flight has cost so far; 0 once its receipt lands.

sub.description: The sub-thread these blocks are of, started from `thread`; none for its own.

oneOf.description: The streaming text or thinking block `index` grew by `append`, the only change since the last notice; the rest of the view stays as it is (spec §3.9).

sub.description: The sub-thread the block is of; none for the thread's own.

oneOf.description: The thread's history is all sent; what follows is live.
The thread's line comments and code review, on open and whenever they change.
The project's memory notes, oldest first.
The files the project's threads changed, the most recent first.
What a run can be given, when this cedia lists it: the models (`cedia models`) and the permission modes (`cedia permissions`). Sent after `Welcome`.
`thread` was forked from `from` and its run is starting.
The project's `/` commands: its skills and the person's.
The project's scheduled runs (`cedia schedules`), `None` when this cedia has none, and the MCP servers in cedia's settings.
What `Request::Restore` moved, and what it left.
What `Request::Rewind` did, or why it did not.
The answer to `Request::Usage`, with the request's `cwd` and `since`.
The answer to `Request::CommitDraft`.
The answer to `Request::Commit`.
The answer to `Request::PrCheck`.
The answer to `Request::Pr`.
The person's MCP servers, and why the change asked for last was refused, if it was.
The answer to `Request::Complete`.
The answer to `Request::InlineEdit`.
The answer to `Request::McpCheck`.
The answer to `Request::Browser`: the project's page, or why there is none (no Chromium found, or it did not start).
The answer to `Request::Git` and `Request::GitAction`: the thread's folder in git, or why there is none (not a git repository).

after.description: The action this answers, once it has finished; none for a plain read.

fetched.description: It fetched first (`Request::Git` `fetch`), so behind is current.

oneOf.description: The answer to `Request::PrView` and `Request::PrAct`: the thread's PR, none when its branch has none, or why it could not be read (`gh` missing or signed out).

acted.description: It answers a `Request::PrAct`, which has finished.

oneOf.description: The answer to `Request::Prs`, or why there is none (`gh` missing or signed out, or no GitHub remote).
The answer to `Request::Issues`, or why there is none (`gh` missing or signed out, or no GitHub remote).
The answer to `Request::Issue`, `Request::IssueAct` and `Request::NewIssue`: the issue as it stands, read again after an action. `number` is none when a new issue was not opened.

acted.description: It answers an action (or a new issue) that `gh` did.

failed.description: Why the action failed; the view is still the issue as it stands.

oneOf.description: The answer to `Request::PrLog`.
The thread was not archived: its worktree has uncommitted changes in `files`, which go when the worktree is removed after archive (spec §8.4). The window asks Archive anyway?

An ask that failed, and why. `thread`: the thread it was about, so the agent pane shows it only there; `settings`: the settings window asked, so it shows there and not in the pane (spec §8.4: inline where it happened).

cwd.description: Where the session that changed it ran.

exists.description: It is still there: a later change, or the worktree's removal, may have taken it away.

thread.description: The thread that changed it last, and its title.

PrAction.description: What the PR block asks of the thread's PR, each through `gh`.

oneOf.description: A comment on the conversation.
A reply in a line comment's thread.
A review with the person's verdict; Approve and RequestChanges only on someone else's PR.
Merges now; `delete_branch` deletes the head after.
Merge when ready on (`method`) or off (none).
Merges the base into the head on GitHub.
Marks a draft ready for review.

run.description: The Actions run it belongs to, whose failed log `Request::PrAct` `log` reads.

PrChip.description: A thread's pull request as the daemon last saw it through `gh` (ARCHITECTURE, Phase C "Watching a thread's pull request"), for the chip on its row and its card.

conflict.description: GitHub cannot merge it into its base without a conflict.

fixing.description: A run the watch started for the PR's head is going or has not pushed yet.

review.description: GitHub's review decision (`approved`, `changes_requested`, `review_required`); none when the repository asks for no review.

PrList.description: The repository's open pull requests, as the list's tabs split them.

state.description: `approved`, `changes_requested`, `commented`; none while asked and not yet reviewed.

PrSummary.description: One open pull request of the project's repository, for the Pull requests list.

review_requested.description: The person's review is asked for.

hunk.description: The diff lines the first comment was made on, ending at its line.

id.description: GitHub's node id, which a reply or Resolve names.

PrView.description: A thread's pull request as the PR block draws it (spec §11 Phase D: review, merge and issues in Cedian), read through the person's own `gh` (`Request::PrView`).

auto_merge.description: The merge method GitHub will use once checks and reviews allow, when merge when ready is on.

behind.description: The base has commits the head does not (`mergeStateStatus` BEHIND).

closes.description: The issues it closes when merged.

comments.description: The conversation's own comments, oldest first.

conflict.description: GitHub cannot merge it without a conflict.

mine.description: The person (`gh`'s login) opened it, so Approve and Request changes are not theirs.

review_decision.description: `approved`, `changes_requested`, `review_required`; none when no review is asked.

reviewers.description: Each reviewer's latest say, and the ones asked who have not said yet.

threads.description: Line comments, grouped as GitHub threads them.

Request.description: From the window to the daemon.

oneOf.description: The project's threads, answered with `Notice::Threads`, and again whenever one changes.
A thread's history so far, then its lines as they arrive.

The window drew one blocks or text notice of the thread. From a window's first ack of a thread on, the daemon keeps at most two of its notices undrawn there, merging the rest (spec §3.9); notices sent before that first ack are not counted.
No more lines for this thread.
One cedia run. With no thread it opens a new one, and the client is sent `Started` and then the run's lines.

effort.description: How hard the writer starts thinking (`cedia --effort`): a level the model lists; none keeps the model's own.

images.description: Image files shown to the writer with the text (`cedia --image`), when cedia lists `images`. cedia stores each by its hash when the run starts, so a pasted image's file needs to last only until then.

model.description: The model this run's writer takes (`cedia -m`); none keeps cedia's choice.

permission.description: What the run may do (`cedia --permission`): a mode from `Notice::Choices`; none keeps cedia's default.

profile.description: For a new thread: the cedia profile its runs take (`coordinator` for the project chat).

worktree.description: For a new thread: run it in a new git worktree of the project.

oneOf.description: The `/` commands a run in the project can take (`cedia commands`), answered with `Notice::Commands` when this cedia lists them.

Where the spend went since `since` (`7d`, `30d` or a day, `YYYY-MM-DD`), in the project at `cwd` or, with none, every project (`cedia usage --json --since`), answered with `Notice::Usage` when this cedia offers `usage`.

Puts the files of `thread`'s last turn that changed files back (`cedia threads undo`), or forward again with `redo`; `force` also moves a file changed since. The client is sent `Restored`, when this cedia offers `threads.restore-json`.
Takes `thread` back to just before its run `n`, from 1, conversation and files together (`cedia threads rewind`); `force` goes past a refusal that allows it. The client is sent `Rewound`.

Edit and resend: a new thread whose conversation is `thread`'s just before `run` (`cedia threads fork`), then `text` as its next run. The client is sent `Forked`, then the run's lines as for an open thread.

images.description: The images the resent message carries, each a file or `sha256:<hex>` for one cedia stored. None keeps the forked run's own (cedia names them in its fork); an empty list sends none.

oneOf.description: A message the running thread sees at its next turn, with its images (`cedia threads send --image`), when cedia lists `threads.send-images`.

Tab completion: the text to insert at `at` in `file` (`cedia complete --json`), answered with `Notice::Completion` carrying the same `id`, when cedia lists `complete`. A newer ask from the same window stops the one before, which gets no answer. Nothing is written; the editor shows the text as ghost text.

text.description: The file as the editor has it, unsaved changes included; none reads it from disk.

oneOf.description: Cmd+K: the new text for a selection of `file` and the patch it makes (`cedia inline-edit --json`), answered with `Notice::InlineEdit` carrying the same `id`, when cedia lists `inline-edit`. Nothing is written; the window shows the patch for the person to accept.

text.description: The file as the editor has it, unsaved changes included; none reads it from disk.

oneOf.description: Ends the thread's run.
Takes back messages the thread has not seen yet, through `cedia threads unsend`.
The person's 👍 or 👎 on the thread, through `cedia threads rate`.

Hides the thread from the list, or brings it back, through `cedia threads archive|unarchive`. Archiving a thread whose worktree has uncommitted changes answers `Notice::ArchiveGuard` and archives nothing, unless `force` (the person said Archive anyway).
Stops following the thread's pull request, or follows it again (Stop watching, Watch PR). Kept across restarts.
Gives the thread the person's title, through `cedia threads rename`.
Deletes the thread for good, its sub-threads and their logs, through `cedia threads delete`. Refused by cedia while it runs.
The project's memory (`~/.cedia/projects/<slug>/memory.jsonl`), answered with `Notice::Memory`.
The files the project's threads changed, answered with `Notice::Outputs`.
The thread's changes since its first snapshot, answered with `Notice::Review`.
A decision on one hunk of the thread's review, answered with the review again.
Replaces the line comments the person has left on the thread's diff and not sent yet. Every window with the thread open gets `Notice::Notes`.
Sends the thread's line comments as its next message (queued when it runs, else a run) and clears them.
Reviews what the thread changed (`cedia review --thread --json`), when this cedia offers `code-review`. The review lands in the thread's `Notice::Notes`.
Dismisses one finding of the thread's review, or takes the dismissal back.
Asks the thread to fix these findings of its review (all of the open ones when empty), as its next message.

What the Background tasks block lists beside the threads: the project's scheduled runs and the MCP servers cedia's settings name. Answered with `Notice::Background`, and again whenever the schedules change.
Pauses or resumes one scheduled run (`cedia schedules pause|resume`); every window showing the project's background gets `Notice::Background`.
Where the thread's folder (its worktree, else the project) stands in git, answered with `Notice::Git`.

fetch.description: Fetch from the remote first (the person opened the Git card), so behind counts what the remote has now.

oneOf.description: Pull or push the thread's folder, then answers `Notice::Git` with where it stands after; a git that fails answers `Notice::Error` for the thread.
The thread's pull request for the PR block, answered with `Notice::PrView`.
Does `action` on the thread's pull request through `gh`, then answers `Notice::PrView` with `acted`; a refusal answers `Notice::Error` for the thread first.
The repository's open pull requests, answered with `Notice::Prs`.

Starts a thread that reviews PR `number`: a new worktree with the PR checked out (`gh pr checkout`), and a first run that reads it and says what it changes. The PR watch never acts on someone else's PR, so the thread does not push to it.
The repository's issues that `filter` picks, answered with `Notice::Issues`.
One issue, answered with `Notice::Issue`.
Does `action` on issue `number` through `gh`, then answers `Notice::Issue` with it after.
Opens a new issue (`gh issue create`), answered with `Notice::Issue` for it.
The end of a failed Actions run's log, answered with `Notice::PrLog`.
The project's page in the shared Chromium, which the daemon starts when none runs. Answered with `Notice::Browser`; from then on the project's runs get the page.

A message for the files `thread` changed in `cwd` (its worktree, else the project), drafted by its writer model (`cedia commit --thread --json`), answered with `Notice::CommitDraft`, when this cedia offers `commit`. Nothing is committed.
Commits `files` of `thread` with the person's `message` (`cedia commit --message --file`), answered with `Notice::Committed`.
Where a pull request from `cwd` would go, or why it cannot (`cedia pr --check`), answered with `Notice::PrPlan`, when this cedia offers `pr`.
Pushes `cwd`'s branch and opens its pull request (`cedia pr`), answered with `Notice::PrOpened`. Sent only after the person said yes to the plan.
The person's MCP servers (`cedia mcp list --json`), answered with `Notice::Mcp`, when this cedia offers `mcp.manage`.
Starts one server as a run would and lists its tools (`cedia mcp check`), answered with `Notice::McpChecked`.
Adds a server, or replaces the one of that name (`cedia mcp add`), answered with `Notice::Mcp`.
Removes a server (`cedia mcp remove`), answered with `Notice::Mcp`.
The `desktop` key of cedia's settings file, answered with `Notice::Settings` and then `Notice::Choices` again (the settings window opens after the window connected).
Sets one key of `desktop`; `null` removes it. Every window gets `Notice::Settings`.

Review.description: A thread's changes from its first snapshot to its last.

base.description: The first snapshot's tree; none when the thread has not written anything.

permission.description: What the run ran under (`cedia --permission`); none from a cedia that did not record it.

Selection.description: A selection in a file, as cedia's `InlineEditRange`: lines and columns from 1, columns in UTF-16 units as the editor counts them; `end` is just past the last character, and an empty selection asks for text inserted there.

role.description: The session's role: `code` for the writer, else a helper such as `triage`, `explore` or `goal`.

Status.description: What a thread's tab shows: cedia's state, corrected by whether a run is alive.

oneOf.description: The project's coordinator opened it and its first run has not started yet.
A run of this thread is in progress.
Stopped by the person.
cedia's last word was `working` but no run is alive: it crashed or the Mac restarted. The thread can go on with `--thread`.
The run ended on a question for the person; their answer goes on with the thread.

Step.description: One step of a thread's todo list.

by.description: The thread that opened this one with `open_thread` (the project's coordinator), for a client to run: it waits `queued` until its first run.

cwd.description: Where the thread's latest session ran: its worktree, when it has one.

last_turn.description: The latest run that changed files: the shadow-git trees before its first write and after its last, what `cedia threads diff|undo|redo` call the thread's turn.

needs_you.description: It finished, failed, was interrupted or asks something since the person last saw it: it counts in the badges until a window opens it.

parent.description: The thread that spawned this one as a sub-thread.

pending.description: Messages no session has been shown yet.

pr.description: Its branch's pull request, while the daemon follows it.

pr_unwatched.description: The person stopped the daemon following this thread's pull request (Stop watching).

profile.description: The profile its runs take unless another is named.

question.description: What the thread asked the person, while it waits in `asking` for the answer.

rating.description: The person's latest 👍 or 👎 on the thread (`cedia threads rate`).

rewound.description: Sessions a rewind dropped (`cedia rewind`): their logs stay, but they are no longer the thread's conversation, so they are not in `sessions`.

root.description: The workspace root it works in, when `open_thread` named one other than the primary (a multi-repo project, `desktop.roots`).

runs.description: The thread's runs in order, each with the prompt that started it: where a fork for edit and resend goes back to (`cedia threads fork`). A rewind's dropped runs are not here.

state.description: cedia's last state. A run that died leaves `working`.

todo.description: The writer's latest list of steps, whole: the thread's progress.

options.description: Two to four choices, the recommended one first; none for a free answer.
